To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the concentrations of free and conjugates of testosterone, 17β-hydroxy-11-oxoandrost-4-en-3-one (11-ketotetosterone, 11-KT) and 17β-hydoxyandrost-4-ene-3,11-dione (11β-hydroxtestosterone, 118HT) were determined by radioimmunoassays throughout the reproductive cycle of brown trout (Salmo trutta).

1) the concentrations of testosterone and its glucuronide are high during the period of spermation in male brown trout; 2) the concentrations of 11-keto-testosterone, and its glucuronides are highest in the period immediately preceding and during the time of spermiation; 3) the concentrations of free and glucuronide forms of 11β-hydorxytestosterone are highest during the same period as 11-ketotesotone; and 4)

the ratio of free: conjugated androgene in male brown trout changes during the annual reproductive cycle and that the highest levels of free testosterone and its conjugates are found at the time of the spawning season.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the seasonal changes in the concentrations of free and conjugates of androgens in brown trout, and their role in the reproductive cycle.
the study of the endocrine regulation of the annual reproductive cycle in the brown trout.

the seasonal changes in plasma concentrations of free and conjugate forms of androgens in brown trout Salmo (trutta) and rainbow trout Oncorhynchus mykiss, and the possible role of these steroids during the annual reproductive cycle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the seasonal changes in free and conjugated testosterone and 11-ketosterone in brown trout are related to the seasonal changes in the reproductive status of the fish, with a peak in free and conjugate androgens coinciding with the period of spermatogenesis and spermiation in late summer.

the plasma concentrations of free and conjugate androgens vary in a characteristic manner during the reproductive cycle of the trout, and that the changes in the concentrations of free androstenes may be due, at least in part, to the activity of glucuronyltransferase.

the brown trout is an 11-ketosteroid fish, but that the presence of significant quantities of 11β-hyroxytestosterone and its glucuronide suggests a possible role for this steroid in the normal functioning and control of the reproductive cycle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the brown trout Salo trutta, like the rainbow trout Salmo gairdneri, has an annual reproductive cycle in which the concentrations of free and conjugate androgens are correlated with the stages of spermatogenesis and the period of sperm release.

the brown trout has a complex and highly regulated reproductive cycle which is controlled by the interplay of several endocrine systems, and that the role of glucuronidation is to modulate the action of the androgens at the target tissues.

in the male brown trout the annual cycle of androgens is as follows: testosterone is the major androgen in the early reproductive period; 11β-hyroxytestosterone is the major androsten in the period of gonadal regression, and 11-ketosterone the major androsterone in the period of spermation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ratio of free: conjugated androgene in the blood of the trout varies with the season.
the ratio of free to conjugated testosterone in plasma of the brown trout Salo trutta is much lower than previously reported.

testosterone and 11-KT are the primary androgens in male salmonids, and that the glucuronic conjugates are not just a byproduct of the metabolism of these androgens but may play a role in the reproductive physiology.
